User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the application, which can be either a patient or the doctor. This entity stores core profile information.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity.

fullName.description: The full name of the user.

email.description: The email address of the user.

phoneNumber.description: The phone number of the user.

dateOfBirth.description: The date of birth of the user.

role.description: The role of the user in the application (e.g., 'patient', 'doctor').

isActive.description: Indicates if the user account is currently active. Doctor can deactivate/delete users.

createdAt.description: The timestamp when the user profile was created.

updatedAt.description: The timestamp when the user profile was last updated.

DoctorProfile.title: DoctorProfile
DoctorProfile.description: Stores specific details and professional information for the single doctor using the platform.

id.description: Unique identifier for the DoctorProfile entity.

userId.description: Reference to the User entity for the doctor. (Relationship: User 1:1 DoctorProfile)

education.description: Details about the doctor's educational background.

practiceLocation.description: The primary geographical location where the doctor practices.

yearsOfExperience.description: The total number of years the doctor has been practicing professionally.

patientsServed.description: The approximate number of patients the doctor has served.

aboutMeSummary.description: A concise summary or biography of the doctor. Longer content is managed via Sanity CMS.

Booking.title: Booking
Booking.description: Manages patient appointment bookings, including type, status, and associated details.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Booking entity.

patientId.description: Reference to the User entity for the patient who made the booking. (Relationship: User 1:N Booking)

doctorId.description: Reference to the User entity for the doctor. (Relationship: User 1:N Booking)

appointmentDateTime.description: The scheduled date and time for the appointment.

type.description: The type of consultation requested (e.g., 'Chat', 'Video', 'Clinic Visit').

status.description: The current status of the booking (e.g., 'Pending', 'Accepted', 'Declined', 'Rescheduled', 'Completed', 'Cancelled').

meetingLink.description: The URL for video conference appointments (e.g., Google Meet link), if applicable.

patientNotes.description: Any specific notes or queries provided by the patient during the booking process.

doctorNotes.description: Any specific notes added by the doctor regarding the booking.

rescheduleReason.description: The reason provided if the booking was rescheduled.

cancellationReason.description: The reason provided if the booking was cancelled.

createdAt.description: The timestamp when the booking was initially created.

updatedAt.description: The timestamp when the booking was last updated or its status changed.

Prescription.title: Prescription
Prescription.description: Stores details of prescriptions issued by the doctor to patients, including medicine items and instructions.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Prescription entity.

patientId.description: Reference to the User entity for the patient receiving the prescription. (Relationship: User 1:N Prescription)

doctorId.description: Reference to the User entity for the doctor who issued the prescription. (Relationship: User 1:N Prescription)

issuedDate.description: The date when the prescription was issued.

generalRemarks.description: Any general remarks or overarching instructions from the doctor for the entire prescription.

medicineItems.description: An array of objects, where each object represents a single medicine prescribed.

createdAt.description: The timestamp when the prescription was created.

MedicineSchedule.title: MedicineSchedule
MedicineSchedule.description: Manages individual medicine dosage schedules for patients, used for reminders and tracking adherence.

id.description: Unique identifier for the MedicineSchedule entity.

prescriptionId.description: Reference to the Prescription entity this schedule belongs to. (Relationship: Prescription 1:N MedicineSchedule)

patientId.description: Reference to the User entity for the patient. (Relationship: User 1:N MedicineSchedule)

medicineName.description: The name of the medicine for which this schedule entry is created.

scheduledDateTime.description: The exact date and time a specific dose of medicine is scheduled to be taken.

dosage.description: The specific dosage amount for this scheduled medicine intake.

taken.description: Indicates whether the patient has marked this specific dose as taken.

reminderSent.description: Indicates whether a notification reminder for this schedule entry has been sent.

createdAt.description: The timestamp when this medicine schedule entry was created.

updatedAt.description: The timestamp when this medicine schedule entry was last updated (e.g., marked as taken).

AppConfig.title: AppConfig
AppConfig.description: Stores global application settings and doctor-specific configurations, such as pricing and clinic details.

id.description: Unique identifier for the AppConfig entity (e.g., a fixed ID like 'global-config').

doctorId.description: Reference to the User entity for the doctor who owns these configurations. (Relationship: User 1:1 AppConfig)

chatPricing.description: The price for a chat consultation.

videoPricing.description: The price for a video consultation.

clinicVisitPricing.description: The price for a direct clinic visit.

clinicAddress.description: The physical address of the doctor's clinic.

clinicMapLink.description: A URL linking to the clinic's location on a map service (e.g., Google Maps).

contactEmail.description: The general contact email address for the clinic or doctor.

contactPhoneNumber.description: The general contact phone number for the clinic or doctor.

globalMessage.description: A message set by the doctor to be displayed globally across the patient-facing application.

unavailableDates.description: An array of specific dates (YYYY-MM-DD) when the doctor is completely unavailable for appointments.

Review.title: Review
Review.description: Captures patient feedback and ratings for the doctor, which can be internally managed or potentially featured as testimonials.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Review entity.

patientId.description: Reference to the User entity for the patient who submitted the review. (Relationship: User 1:N Review)

doctorId.description: Reference to the User entity for the doctor being reviewed. (Relationship: User 1:N Review)

rating.description: The rating given by the patient, typically on a scale (e.g., 1 to 5 stars).

comment.description: The textual feedback or detailed comment provided by the patient.

reviewDate.description: The date when the review was submitted.

isApprovedForTestimonials.description: Indicates if this review has been approved by the doctor for consideration as a public testimonial (managed via Sanity CMS).

createdAt.description: The timestamp when the review was created.

Notification.title: Notification
Notification.description: Represents a notification to be delivered to a user, typically stored in Realtime Database for real-time updates.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Notification entity.

userId.description: Reference to the User entity who is the recipient of this notification. (Relationship: User 1:N Notification)

message.description: The descriptive content of the notification message.

type.description: The category or type of notification (e.g., 'booking_accepted', 'prescription_added', 'medicine_reminder').

relatedEntityId.description: Optional: Reference to the ID of the entity that triggered this notification (e.g., a Booking ID, Prescription ID).

isRead.description: Indicates whether the recipient user has viewed or acknowledged this notification.

createdAt.description: The timestamp when the notification was generated and sent.

definition.description: Stores core user profile information for both patients and the doctor. The document ID matches the Firebase Auth UID. Includes a 'role' field (patient/doctor) for basic access control.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique Firebase Auth UID of the user (patient or doctor).

definition.description: A dedicated collection for Database Access Control (DBAC) to explicitly mark the single doctor. The existence of a document here (whose ID is the doctor's UID) grants 'doctor' privileges in security rules, promoting Authorization Independence. The document itself can be empty or contain minimal identifying info.

params.name: doctorId
params.description: The unique Firebase Auth UID of the single doctor.

definition.description: Stores the specific professional profile details for the single doctor. The document ID is the doctor's UID. Includes 'userId' field matching the doctor's UID for Authorization Independence.

params.name: doctorId
params.description: The unique Firebase Auth UID of the single doctor.

definition.description: Stores global application settings and doctor-specific configurations (e.g., pricing, clinic details). This is a singleton document whose ID is the doctor's UID. Includes 'doctorId' field for Authorization Independence.

params.name: doctorId
params.description: The unique Firebase Auth UID of the single doctor.

params.name: patientId
params.description: The unique Firebase Auth UID of the patient.

params.name: bookingId
params.description: The unique identifier for the booking.

definition.description: Stores prescriptions issued to a specific patient. Patient can only access their own prescriptions. Includes denormalized 'patientId' and 'doctorId' for Authorization Independence.

params.name: patientId
params.description: The unique Firebase Auth UID of the patient.

params.name: prescriptionId
params.description: The unique identifier for the prescription.

definition.description: Manages individual medicine dosage schedules for a patient. Patient can only access their own schedules. Includes denormalized 'patientId' and 'doctorId' (from Prescription) for Authorization Independence, enabling direct security rule checks without fetching parent documents.

params.name: patientId
params.description: The unique Firebase Auth UID of the patient.

params.name: medicineScheduleId
params.description: The unique identifier for the medicine schedule entry.

definition.description: Captures patient feedback and ratings for the doctor. Patients can create and manage their own reviews, while the doctor can read all. Includes denormalized 'patientId' and 'doctorId' for Authorization Independence.

params.name: reviewId
params.description: The unique identifier for the review.

firestore.reasoning:
The recommended Firestore structure prioritizes Authorization Independence, Structural Segregation, and DBAC (Database Access Control) to achieve simple, robust, and debuggable security rules. All collections maintain a homogeneous security posture, meaning documents within a single collection share the same access patterns. 

**Authorization Independence via Denormalization:**
- The core principle of avoiding `get()` calls in security rules is achieved by denormalizing authorization-critical fields directly into the documents where they are needed. For entities like `Booking`, `Prescription`, and `Review`, the `patientId` and `doctorId` are explicitly stored within each document. This allows security rules to evaluate access based solely on `request.auth.uid` against these fields, without needing to fetch parent documents or related entities.
- Specifically for `MedicineSchedule`, the `doctorId` will be denormalized from the `Prescription` entity. While `prescriptionId` and `patientId` are already present, including `doctorId` directly in `MedicineSchedule` documents allows the doctor to query and manage all medicine schedules without needing to perform a `get()` on the parent prescription, thereby simplifying rules and supporting atomic operations.
- The `User` collection itself stores the `role` ('patient' or 'doctor'), and a dedicated `/roles_doctor/{doctorId}` collection is used for explicit role-based access control for the single doctor. The mere existence of a document in this collection with the `request.auth.uid` as its ID grants doctor privileges, adhering to the 'existence over content' DBAC strategy.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):**
- **Structural Segregation** is heavily utilized to support secure `list` operations. Patient-specific data (`Booking`, `Prescription`, `MedicineSchedule`) is nested under `/patients/{patientId}/...`. This structure inherently restricts a patient's queries to their own data (`/patients/$(request.auth.uid)/bookings`) and allows security rules to easily verify that the `patientId` in the path matches `request.auth.uid`.
- For the doctor, who needs to view all bookings, prescriptions, and schedules across all patients, the security rules will grant access to these subcollections based on the `doctorId` field within the documents (e.g., `resource.data.doctorId == request.auth.uid`) or by checking the `/roles_doctor` collection. This allows the doctor to perform collection group queries or specific collection queries that are properly indexed and secured.
- The top-level `/reviews` collection allows patients to create their own reviews and the doctor to read all reviews, with authorization enforced by `patientId` and `doctorId` fields denormalized within each `Review` document.
- Singleton documents for `DoctorProfile` and `AppConfig` are identified by the doctor's `userId` as their document ID, ensuring that only the authenticated doctor can access and modify these critical settings.
